hook: Synthetic vesicles swim away from a chemical signal with no catalyst or outside energy.
summary: A minimal polymer vesicle shows negative chemotaxis, moving away from a chemical cue because its hydrophobic membrane domains rearrange and shift interfacial tension. This offers a molecular mechanism for artificial motility that mimics cytoskeletal remodeling. The abstract gives no quantitative performance, and the system is a simplified lab model, far from a living protocell.
title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles.
